options.E: Retinal fibrosis EXPLANATION & RATIONALE CORRECT OPTION: A DIABETIC MACULAR EDEMA (DME) is the MOST COMMON CAUSE OF VISION LOSS in diabetic retinopathy across both Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes. Treated with intravitreal Anti-VEGF. INCORRECT OPTIONS ANALYSIS • Vitreous hemorrhage causes sudden vision loss, but DME affects a far greater total patient population. ■ HIGH-YIELD CLINICAL PEARL • #1 cause of vision loss in diabetic retinopathy: Diabetic Macular Edema (DME). • First-line therapy: Intravitreal Anti-VEGF. ■ EXAM TRAP / DO NOT MISS DME can occur at any stage of diabetic retinopathy. ■ EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVE Identify diabetic macular edema as the leading cause of vision impairment in patients with diabetic retinopathy.

questions.question: All of the following are true regarding optic neuritis EXCEPT:

options.A: Can present with painful eye movement
options.B: Oral steroids are the initial treatment of choice to reduce the duration of the disease
options.D: Ishihara test is useful in diagnosis
options.E: Fundus examination is typically unremarkable EXPLANATION & RATIONALE CORRECT OPTION: B Statement B ('Oral steroids are initial treatment') is FALSE: The ONTT trial proved oral prednisone alone doubles the rate of recurrent optic neuritis. IV methylprednisolone is standard. INCORRECT OPTIONS ANALYSIS • Pain on movement, female predilection, red desaturation, and normal fundus are all true of optic neuritis. ■ HIGH-YIELD CLINICAL PEARL • Standard-dose oral prednisone alone doubles the risk of recurrent optic neuritis! ■ EXAM TRAP / DO NOT MISS Never prescribe oral steroids alone as initial monotherapy for optic neuritis. ■ EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVE Reiterate that oral corticosteroids alone are contraindicated in acute optic neuritis because they increase recurrence rates.

questions.question: All of the following are signs of non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy except:

options.E: Hard exudates EXPLANATION & RATIONALE CORRECT OPTION: C NEW VESSELS AT THE DISC (NVD) defines PROLIFERATIVE diabetic retinopathy (PDR) and is NOT a sign of non-proliferative retinopathy. Hemorrhages, microaneurysms, and hard exudates belong to NPDR. INCORRECT OPTIONS ANALYSIS • Hemorrhages, microaneurysms, cotton wool spots, and hard exudates are authentic signs of NPDR. ■ HIGH-YIELD CLINICAL PEARL • Neovascularization of the disc (NVD) = Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy. ■ EXAM TRAP / DO NOT MISS NVD is high-risk PDR requiring prompt laser photocoagulation. ■ EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVE Recognize neovascularization of the disc (NVD) as the hallmark of proliferative diabetic retinopathy, distinguishing it from non-proliferative signs.

questions.question: All of the following are seen in thyroid eye disease EXCEPT:

options.E: Bilateral proptosis EXPLANATION & RATIONALE CORRECT OPTION: C PTOSIS is NOT seen in thyroid eye disease; thyroid eye disease produces eyelid RETRACTION and lid lag. Ptosis suggests coexisting myasthenia gravis. INCORRECT OPTIONS ANALYSIS • Proptosis, lid retraction, and lid lag are classic for thyroid orbitopathy. ■ HIGH-YIELD CLINICAL PEARL • Graves' = Lid Retraction; Myasthenia Gravis = Ptosis. ■ EXAM TRAP / DO NOT MISS Ptosis in a Graves' patient mandates checking for Myasthenia Gravis. ■ EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVE Confirm that thyroid eye disease characteristically produces upper eyelid retraction rather than ptosis.

questions.question: Which is TRUE regarding juvenile idiopathic arthritis?

options.A: Patients with the systemic onset subtype have the highest risk for ocular complications
options.B: The most common presentation of ocular involvement is eye redness and photophobia
options.C: Regular screening is not needed in asymptomatic patients
options.D: The associated ocular manifestation is recurrent posterior uveitis
options.E: The long-term complications of recurrent ocular inflammation are cataract and glaucoma EXPLANATION & RATIONALE CORRECT OPTION: E Statement E is TRUE: The long-term sight-threatening complications of recurrent untreated chronic anterior uveitis in JIA are CATARACT and GLAUCOMA (along with band keratopathy). INCORRECT OPTIONS ANALYSIS • Systemic onset JIA has minimal uveitis; JIA uveitis is asymptomatic without redness; regular screening is mandatory; inflammation is anterior, not posterior. ■ HIGH-YIELD CLINICAL PEARL • JIA Complications: Band keratopathy, complicated cataract, secondary glaucoma. ■ EXAM TRAP / DO NOT MISS Screen asymptomatic children with oligoarticular JIA every 3 months with slit lamp. ■ EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVE Identify cataract and glaucoma as the primary long-term blinding complications of chronic anterior uveitis in juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

questions.question: All of the following are signs of non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy except:

options.B: Neovascularization of the disc (NVD) EXPLANATION & RATIONALE CORRECT OPTION: B NEOVASCULARIZATION OF THE DISC (NVD) defines PROLIFERATIVE diabetic retinopathy and is absent in non-proliferative disease. INCORRECT OPTIONS ANALYSIS • Retinal hemorrhages belong to non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. ■ HIGH-YIELD CLINICAL PEARL • Neovascularization = Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy. ■ EXAM TRAP / DO NOT MISS Any pathological new vessels shift the diagnosis to proliferative retinopathy. ■ EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVE Reinforce that neovascularization defines proliferative diabetic retinopathy and is absent in non-proliferative disease.

questions.question: Which of the following is associated with thyroid eye disease?

options.E: Heterochromia EXPLANATION & RATIONALE CORRECT OPTION: D PROPTOSIS is the cardinal manifestation of thyroid eye disease. INCORRECT OPTIONS ANALYSIS • Ptosis, anisocoria, fungal keratitis, and heterochromia are not features of thyroid orbitopathy. ■ HIGH-YIELD CLINICAL PEARL • Thyroid orbitopathy = Proptosis + Lid Retraction. ■ EXAM TRAP / DO NOT MISS Smoking drastically increases the severity of thyroid orbitopathy. ■ EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVE Reiterate proptosis as the hallmark physical manifestation of thyroid eye disease.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding diabetic retinopathy?

options.A: The proliferative stage is an early stage of the disease
options.B: The earliest sign is retinal hemorrhages
options.C: Patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus need screening at the time of diagnosis
options.D: The presence of new vessels is an indication for treatment
options.E: Macular edema is an uncommon cause of vision loss in diabetic patients EXPLANATION & RATIONALE CORRECT OPTION: D Statement D is TRUE: The presence of NEW VESSELS (NVD or NVE) defines proliferative diabetic retinopathy and is an absolute INDICATION FOR TREATMENT with panretinal photocoagulation or anti-VEGF therapy. INCORRECT OPTIONS ANALYSIS • Proliferative stage is advanced; microaneurysms are the earliest sign; Type 1 DM is screened 5 years after diagnosis; macular edema is the most common cause of vision loss. ■ HIGH-YIELD CLINICAL PEARL • New vessels (PDR) mandate urgent Panretinal Photocoagulation or Anti-VEGF therapy. ■ EXAM TRAP / DO NOT MISS Type 1 screening = 5 years post-diagnosis; Type 2 screening = at time of diagnosis. ■ EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVE Recognize that neovascularization defines proliferative diabetic retinopathy and mandates urgent treatment with panretinal photocoagulation or anti-VEGF therapy.
